setup: Load the sled and clear the lane ahead
Hands on the poles at chest height
Arms nearly straight and locked in place
Lean in with a long, straight body line
execution: Push the floor back with the balls of your feet
Keep your hips low and your back flat
Breathe steadily and keep the sled moving
faults: Going out too fast and stalling
Hips piking up and back rounding

notes: Push on a surface meant for sleds, in shoes with good grip.
Keep the lane clear of people and kit before you start.
Heavy pushes raise breathing and heart rate fast. Rest until your breathing settles before the next length.
The logged load is the plates added. The sled's own weight and floor friction aren't counted, so loads aren't comparable between sleds or gyms. HYROX race weights include the sled.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move
Chest pain, faintness or unusual breathlessness

regressions.name: Lighter sled or shorter lengths
regressions.reason: Learn the body angle and step rhythm before adding weight.

progressions.name: Race-weight pushes on carpet
progressions.reason: Practise at HYROX weight and on a high-friction surface before race day.

progressions.name: Run, sled push, run
progressions.reason: Practises pushing on tired legs, as in a HYROX race.

substitutions.name: Leg press
substitutions.reason: Leg drive when there's no sled track. Not a conditioning match.

substitutions.name: Dumbbell walking lunge
substitutions.reason: Loaded single-leg drive over a distance.

substitutions.name: Wall drive
substitutions.reason: Drills the leaning body angle and short steps with no equipment.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view, figure facing right, camera at hip height. Locomotion: the floor scrolls left while the figure and sled stay centred (ground.scrollPerCycle about 0.55 of body height for two steps). Sled with upright poles in front of the figure.

keyPositions.label: Near-leg drive
keyPositions.describe: Body leaning about 45° from vertical in a straight line from the rear ankle through hip and shoulder to head. Near leg extended behind, pushing off the ball of the foot with the heel up. Far leg forward with the knee under the hip and the foot about to land. Arms nearly straight, hands on the poles at about chest height. Head neutral, eyes down and ahead.

keyPositions.label: Switch
keyPositions.describe: Mid-stride, feet passing under the hips. Body angle and hip height unchanged. Arms unchanged. Sled has moved forward by about one short step.

keyPositions.label: Far-leg drive
keyPositions.describe: Mirror of Near-leg drive: far leg extended behind pushing off the ball of the foot, near leg forward with the knee under the hip.

ikHints: Hands fixed to the sled poles in every frame
Stance foot planted on its forefoot while the floor scrolls under it
Hip height constant within about ±2% of body height
guideBrief.barPath: Not applicable. The sled moves horizontally at a steady speed; shown by floor scroll
emphasise: Steady forward lean with a straight body line
Short steps, pushing off the balls of the feet
Arms stay fixed; the legs do the work

uncertain.note: 'distance' is a proposed addition (research §4.4). The current MeasurementSchema only allows reps and duration. Needs the schema change and ADR before this entry validates.
'sled' is a proposed EquipmentKind (research §4.4). It is not in packages/schemas yet.
Little research on muscle use in sled pushing. Secondary muscles are reasoned from the movement, not measured.

Uses a stride tempo (stepMs, stepsPerCycle) instead of down/hold/up, which doesn't fit locomotion. The step time is slowed for readability; real heavy pushes may step faster. Step length and scroll distance are estimates.
Approximate drawing targets. Body lean and hand height vary with sled pole height and load.

Hand and arm position varies. Centr suggests forearms on the poles; many athletes push with straight arms on high or low handles. The entry shows nearly straight arms at chest height as one reasonable default.
